title: The truth shall make you free (John 8:31–32)
word: The truth shall make you free
hook: freedom comes from continuing in his word

segments.voice: Yesterday, the golden lamps of Tabernacles and the light of the world. Your line was not in darkness. Did you take just the next step you could see? Day five hundred eight.

The truth shall make you free. It's carved in stone over library doors and on university buildings across the country. It's printed on mugs and tattooed on forearms. It gets quoted at graduations, in courtrooms, in speeches about free speech and open government. Almost always it's used to mean: information is good, so dig it up. That's not nothing. But the line has a first half that almost never makes it onto the building. Today we read the whole sentence, and the argument it started in the temple.
screen: `CARVED OVER LIBRARY DOORS.` → `QUOTED AT GRADUATIONS.` → `THE MISSING FIRST HALF.`

segments.voice: John tells us Jesus is speaking to people who had come to believe in him. Here's the whole sentence, in the Douay-Rheims: "If you continue in my word, you shall be my disciples indeed. And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free." It begins with if. If you continue, or as older Bibles say, abide, stay, make your home in my word. Freedom doesn't come at the start; it comes from staying. And truth here isn't first of all a fact you look up. In John's Gospel, truth is close to a person: later Jesus will say, I am the way, and the truth, and the life. Knowing the truth means coming to know him, over time, by staying. His listeners bristle. We are Abraham's children, they say, and we've never been slaves to anyone. Jesus answers that he means another kind of slavery: "whosoever committeth sin, is the servant of sin." The thing you can't stop doing. The lie you have to keep up. The habit that runs you. And then: if the Son makes you free, you shall be free indeed. Saint John Paul the Second built a whole letter on moral life, The Splendor of Truth, around this connection. Freedom, he wrote, isn't doing whatever we like; it depends on truth and grows by living in it. On an ordinary day, it can be very small. Every lie needs guarding. Every truth you finally tell is one less thing to guard.
screen: `IF YOU CONTINUE IN MY WORD.` · `TRUTH: A PERSON, NOT ONLY A FACT.` · `THE SERVANT OF SIN.` · `FREEDOM DEPENDS ON TRUTH.` · then, large: `THE TRUTH SHALL MAKE YOU FREE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: tell one small truth you've avoided. Settle, and breathe. Let one thing come to mind that you haven't said. Not the biggest secret. Something small. I'm the one who broke it. I'm actually not fine. I can't make it on Friday. I liked your idea more than I said. Notice how much effort it has taken to keep it unsaid. Picture saying it, plainly and kindly. If you pray, you can ask for the courage to say it. If you don't, just choose when you'll say it. The bell holds the time.
The truth shall make you free. Jesus's promise to those who continue in his word. In John, truth is close to a person. Today's word.

segments.voice: Your line: the truth sets free. Today, say the small true thing, and notice what you no longer have to guard. Day five hundred eight.

howItsDone: Catholics hear John 8:31–42 at a weekday Mass in the fifth week of Lent, and the Church's moral teaching, especially Saint John Paul II's Veritatis Splendor, draws on it to link freedom with truth.

original.note: Greek: truth (John 8:32), a key word in John's Gospel; Jesus will say, I am the truth.

trapdoor: what you thought: a slogan about information.
what it means: freedom comes from staying in Christ's word, and the opposite of freedom is slavery to sin.
what a scholar hears: menō (continue, abide) is one of John's favorite verbs; Veritatis Splendor argues freedom depends on truth.

notes: John 8 contains sharp exchanges; the script names the listeners as 'people who had come to believe in him' (8:31) and avoids collective labels. Confirm the framing (cf. Nostra Aetate 4).
'Carved over library doors and on university buildings' is general; no specific building named. Confirm.
Veritatis Splendor paraphrased (freedom depends on truth; VS 34, 84–87 cite John 8:32). Confirm.
Lectionary: John 8:31–42 on Wednesday of the Fifth Week of Lent. Confirm.
'Make your home in my word' as a gloss on menō: confirm.
